topics.title: Stonehenge altar stone mystery narrows
topics.summary: Geologists have ruled out north-east Scotland as the source of Stonehenge’s altar stone. New testing narrows the search toward other parts of Scotland, northern England or Ireland without yet settling the prehistoric puzzle.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you joined the Stonehenge detective team, would you look for clues in rocks, old maps, boat routes, or something completely different?

topics.title: A Roman-era ruler gets a fresh look
topics.summary: An archaeologist has proposed that Verica, the ruler linked to Rome’s AD43 invasion of Britain, may have been a queen rather than a king. Other experts remain cautious, making it a lively historical debate.
topics.discussionPrompt: History can change when someone rereads old clues. What mystery from the past would you most like historians to solve next?

topics.title: France sees a nationwide strike day
topics.summary: Workers and students joined demonstrations across France over living costs, education and public spending. Rail, air traffic, schools and other services faced disruption as unions coordinated industrial action.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a city has a big strike day, what small kindness helps people most: sharing travel tips, flexible schedules, bringing snacks, or checking on neighbours?

topics.title: European groups question data-centre growth
topics.summary: Campaigners in several European countries are preparing demonstrations over the rapid expansion of data centres. Their concerns include electricity, water, land use and how communities share in the benefits of digital infrastructure.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a huge data centre were proposed near you, what would you ask about first: jobs, power use, water, noise, or who gets to decide?

topics.title: Britain considers rules for pavement-blocking ebikes
topics.summary: UK ministers are considering measures aimed at rental ebikes left blocking pavements. The discussion is balancing greener short trips with safe, accessible sidewalks for pedestrians and mobility-device users.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is the nicest way to keep shared bikes handy without turning the sidewalk into an obstacle course?

topics.title: Bank of England raises its interest rate
topics.summary: The Bank of England raised its main interest rate to 4%, its first increase in more than three years. The move reflects concern about inflation and will affect borrowers, savers and wider household budgeting.
topics.discussionPrompt: When money gets more expensive to borrow, what old-fashioned budget habit suddenly seems smart again?

topics.title: BT announces nearly 8,000 job cuts
topics.summary: Telecoms company BT said it will cut almost 8,000 jobs as part of a broader cost-saving programme. The announcement arrives alongside reported profits and a rising share price, renewing debate about change at large employers.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big company says it is getting leaner, what should it protect first: service quality, staff retraining, local jobs, or future innovation?

topics.title: Developing-country debt reaches a record
topics.summary: World Bank data shows the debt of developing countries has reached a record $9.4 trillion. The figures highlight the pressure interest costs can place on public services, infrastructure and climate-resilience investment.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a community suddenly had more room in its budget, where should it spend first: schools, clinics, roads, clean energy, or something else?

topics.title: Australian doctor balances football and charity work
topics.summary: AFLW midfielder Dr Lulu Pullar is preparing for finals while working as a doctor and running a charity. Her story highlights how elite sport can sit alongside service, study and community projects.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is the most impressive two-hat combination: athlete and doctor, musician and teacher, baker and coder, or another pairing?

topics.title: Hijikata stuns Djokovic in Paris
topics.summary: Australia’s Rinky Hijikata beat Novak Djokovic in a surprise Paris Masters result. Djokovic praised his opponent’s performance, while the upset gave tennis fans another reminder that momentum can shift quickly.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes an underdog win so satisfying: surprise, persistence, a perfect day, or seeing a familiar favorite get a real challenge?
